program_name: Civil Engineering (official Italian name: Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Civile). Two-year Master's degree (120 ECTS) of the University of Trento, run by the Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering (DICAM). The programme is articulated into four curricula: 'Strutture' (Structures), 'Costruzioni in legno e strutture esistenti' (Timber construction and existing structures, previously called 'Riabilitazione'/Rehabilitation), 'Digital Civil Infrastructure', and 'Progettazione integrata digitale BIM based per le costruzioni' (BIM-based integrated digital design for construction).
teaching_language: MIXED - English and Italian, and the programme CANNOT be completed entirely in English. This is case (3) in the field definition ('English and Italian'), and in UniTrento's own administrative classification it is treated as an ITALIAN-LANGUAGE degree programme. Evidence: (a) the English course page's 'IN SHORT' box literally states 'LANGUAGE: English Italian'; (b) the Programme Regulations issued by Rectoral Decree no. 637 of 13/07/2026 state 'LINGUA IN CUI SI TIENE IL CORSO: italiano e inglese' (language in which the course is held: Italian and English); (c) the English programme overview page says only 'Part of the lectures are delivered in English'; (d) most decisively, the 2026/2027 university-wide admission call for non-EU applicants is titled 'Bando unico di Ateneo per l'ammissione ai corsi di laurea magistrale IN LINGUA ITALIANA' and lists 'Ingegneria civile (Classe LM23R)' among the fourteen Italian-taught master's programmes, which triggers a compulsory Italian B2 requirement for non-EU applicants. Course-by-course picture from the official 2026/2027 manifesti degli studi: in every one of the four curricula the compulsory core is delivered in Italian - e.g. 'Dinamica e plasticita delle strutture', 'Geotecnica e fondazioni', 'Costruzioni in CA e CAP', 'Costruzioni in acciaio e resistenti al fuoco', 'Costruzione di ponti con Laboratorio', 'Costruzioni di infrastrutture stradali e ferroviarie con Laboratorio', 'Teoria e progetto di strutture con Laboratorio', 'Monitoraggio delle strutture civili con Laboratorio', 'Opere di sostegno'. A minority of courses are English-taught and keep their English title in the Italian manifesto - typically 'Risk analysis and structural reliability', 'Machine learning for wireless structural health monitoring', 'Metastructures', 'Mechanics of solids and structures under extreme conditions', 'Optimization methods for electromagnetic diagnostics of civil infrastructures', 'Digital urban planning', 'Decision Support Systems for Safety and Security', 'Array Antenna Theory and Synthesis Methods', 'Ground Penetrating Radar Theory and Applications', 'Surface Electromagnetics for Wireless Communications and Sensing'; several of these (marked ***) are shared with the Dortmund/Nantes/Trento triple Master's degree MS2. Two Strutture courses carry the explicit note 'in lingua inglese e con continuo supporto in lingua italiana' (in English with continuous support in Italian), and 'Modellazione e simulazione di strutture con Laboratorio' adds 'con Laboratorio in lingua italiana'. Even the 'Digital Civil Infrastructure' curriculum, which has an English name and the highest share of English courses, keeps an Italian-taught compulsory backbone. The final thesis may be written in Italian or in English. CONCLUSION FOR SCOPE PURPOSES: this is NOT an English-taught programme; it is an Italian-language LM-23 with a substantial English-taught component and cannot be finished without Italian. [uncertain]
campus: Trento. Teaching takes place at the seat of the Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering (DICAM), Via Mesiano 77, 38123 Trento (Mesiano campus). Student support office for the programme is also at Via Mesiano 77.
degree_class: LM-23 (Ingegneria Civile / Civil Engineering), activated under Ministerial Decree of 19/12/2023 no. 1649. In the university-wide non-EU admission call the class is written as 'LM23R'. 120 ECTS over 2 years, 12 exams in total.
admission_type: TWO DIFFERENT REGIMES. (1) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: OPEN ACCESS ('accesso libero' / the English course page shows 'ACCESS: Free'). There is no numerus clausus, no TOLC and no entrance examination; instead each applicant must pass a verification of the admission requirements by submitting an online admission request ('richiesta di ammissione') to the Student Support Service, which checks the degree class, the ECTS thresholds, the weighted average and the English requirement, and may call the applicant to an oral interview. (2) Non-EU citizens living outside Italy: RESTRICTED ACCESS with a reserved quota of 5 places, allocated through the university-wide public selection 'Bando unico di Ateneo per l'ammissione ai corsi di laurea magistrale in lingua italiana' for a.y. 2026/2027 (Rectoral Decree, protocol 1419|2025|RET-16/12/2025). Selection is a document-based merit evaluation scored out of 100 with a minimum eligibility threshold of 50/100, plus an optional online interview; unassigned reserved places are released to European and equivalent candidates. No admission test, no TOLC and no SAT are used in either regime.
academic_requirements: CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (Programme Regulations 2026, Art. 2). Route (a): hold a first-cycle (Bachelor's) degree in Italian class L-7 (Civil and Environmental Engineering) ex M.D. 270/04 or class 8 ex M.D. 509/99. Route (b): hold a first-cycle degree in a different class and have acquired minimum ECTS in specific scientific-disciplinary sectors (new SSD codes with former codes in brackets): at least 20 ECTS among MATH-02/A (MAT/02), MATH-02/B (MAT/03), MATH-03/A (MAT/05), MATH-03/B (MAT/06), MATH-04/A (MAT/07), MATH-05/A (MAT/08); at least 18 ECTS among CHEM-03/A (CHIM/03), CHEM-05/A (CHIM/06), CHEM-06/A (CHIM/07), PHYS-01/A (FIS/01), PHYS-04/A (FIS/02), PHYS-04/A (FIS/03), PHYS-02/A (FIS/04), PHYS-05/A (FIS/05), PHYS-05/B (FIS/06), PHYS-06/A (FIS/07), PHYS-06/B (FIS/08); at least 24 ECTS among CEAR-01/A (ICAR/01), CEAR-01/B (ICAR/02), CEAR-03/A (ICAR/04), CEAR-04/A (ICAR/06), CEAR-05/A (ICAR/07), CEAR-06/A (ICAR/08), CEAR-07/A (ICAR/09), CEAR-08/A (ICAR/10), CEAR-08/B (ICAR/11), CEAR-10/A (ICAR/17), IIND-01/D (ING-IND/04), IIND-01/F (ING-IND/06), IIND-07/A (ING-IND/10), IIND-07/B (ING-IND/11), IIND-02/A (ING-IND/13), IIND-03/A (ING-IND/14), IMAT-01/A (ING-IND/22), OF WHICH at least 9 ECTS must be in CEAR-06/A (ICAR/08), IIND-01/D (ING-IND/04), IIND-02/A (ING-IND/13) or IIND-03/A (ING-IND/14). Route (c): holders of pre-ECTS Italian qualifications or of foreign qualifications recognised as suitable are assessed by the Teaching Area Committee (Commissione di Area Didattica), which compares the content of the courses taken with the sectors listed under route (b). MINIMUM GRADE: a weighted average of the examinations taken for the Bachelor's degree (final exam excluded) of at least 22/30 or equivalent. Applicants with a weighted average of 24/30 or higher are admitted directly; applicants between 22/30 and 23.99/30 are admitted only after passing an oral interview assessing the adequacy of their personal preparation; applicants below 22/30 are excluded. NO CONDITIONAL ENROLMENT: 'Non e prevista l'iscrizione con debito formativo' - enrolment carrying an academic debt is not allowed; missing curricular requirements must be made up beforehand by enrolling in Single Courses for Master's Degrees (Corsi singoli) and passing the exams before the enrolment deadline, and additional credits (crediti formativi aggiuntivi) may be prescribed by the Committee. APPLICATION THRESHOLD: students of other departments or universities may submit the request for evaluation of the curricular requirements only after having earned at least 150 ECTS. NON-EU QUOTA AND SCORING (2026/2027 university call, Annex 1 table): 5 reserved places for Ingegneria Civile (LM23R); merit requirement assessed as 'Valutazione della media delle votazioni e dei tempi di laurea'; personal preparation 'Valutazione tramite colloquio' (evaluated through an interview); prior-career knowledge assessed in the areas of geometry, mathematical analysis, numerical analysis, organic chemistry, chemical foundations of technology, experimental physics, condensed-matter physics, industrial applied physics, environmental applied physics, materials science and technology, hydraulics, topography and cartography, mathematical physics, structural mechanics, building architecture, technical drawing, and drawing and methods of industrial engineering. Total score out of 100 with a minimum admission score of 50/100; ties broken in favour of the younger candidate. Non-EU applicants who have not yet graduated may apply provided the degree is obtained by 30 June 2026, and may apply to at most 2 UniTrento programmes. STUDY PATH: the curriculum must be indicated at enrolment and may be changed later provided all compulsory courses of the chosen curriculum are completed; 12 ECTS are free-choice; there are no prerequisite (propedeuticita) rules and no blocking rules; part-time enrolment is NOT available; a student who does not acquire at least 30 ECTS within two academic years forfeits their student status (decadenza).
language_requirements: ENGLISH - MANDATORY FOR EVERYONE, CEFR B2. Programme Regulations 2026, Art. 2.3.d: to be admitted the student must hold proven English competence at least at level B2. It can be evidenced by: an international certificate of equivalent or higher level recognised by DICAM (the department publishes a dedicated PDF list, 'Certificazioni internazionali di inglese riconosciute dal Dipartimento di Ingegneria Civile, Ambientale e Meccanica'); or a self-declaration of having completed a degree programme taught in English; or a self-declaration of having passed the English language test of the UniTrento Language Centre (CLA) or of another university; or a self-declaration of being a native English speaker. Passing a university English exam at B2 during the Bachelor's is also accepted. MAKE-UP ROUTE: applicants who cannot certify B2 may sit the English test organised by UniTrento at the CLA - written part in person in Trento, oral part online. Six sessions were published for 2026: registration 27 March-20 April (written 27 April 14:30, oral 8 May); 20 April-15 May (written 25 May, oral 5 June); 16 May-25 June (written 6 July, oral 17 July); 26 June-21 August (written 2 September, oral 11 September); 24 August-2 October (written 12 October, oral 23 October); 5 October-13 November (written 23 November 14:30, oral 4 December). For non-EU applicants under the university-wide call, Note 3 of the call lists the accepted proofs of English at B2 or above specifically for Ingegneria Civile (LM23R): being a native English speaker (defined as having completed at least two cycles of education in that language), being a citizen of a country whose official language is English, holding an internationally recognised certificate at B2 or above from the CLA list, having completed a Bachelor's degree whose official language of instruction is English, or presenting a transcript of records clearly attesting a university English exam passed at level B2 or above (a transcript without an explicit level is not sufficient). ITALIAN - REQUIRED IN PRACTICE FOR MOST APPLICANTS. (1) Non-EU citizens living abroad: Italian at CEFR B2 is a compulsory admission requirement of the 2026/2027 call ('La dimostrazione della conoscenza della lingua italiana e uno dei requisiti di ammissione, in mancanza del quale non e possibile essere ammessi'). It can be proved with a CLIQ-system certificate (CILS, CELI, PLIDA, ROMA3); with an Italian secondary-school diploma from Italian state or state-recognised schools abroad; with one of the final secondary qualifications listed in Annex 2 of the yearly ministerial circular; with Argentinian complementary certificates attesting at least 5 years of Italian teaching under Law 210/1999; with the Diploma di lingua e cultura italiana of the Universities for Foreigners of Perugia or Siena; or by passing the CISIA Italian L2 test with a score of at least 52/72 (120 minutes, three parts - listening, reading, language structures, 72 questions). The deadline for taking the CISIA Italian L2 test at institutions other than UniTrento was 4 March 2026, and UniTrento organised its own ad hoc CISIA session on 26 March 2026. The Italian check is pass/fail and does not contribute to the ranking score. (2) All other non-native Italian speakers: Programme Regulations Art. 2 provide that candidates whose mother tongue is not Italian, who intend to attend a curriculum not delivered entirely in English or who have not completed at least one cycle of secondary education in Italian, must have their Italian verified - by an international certificate recognised by the University, by self-declaring a university exam passed in Italian, or by passing a written test or interview with the Teaching Area Committee. The Italian admission page states this as Italian at least at level B2 for anyone choosing a curriculum with compulsory activities in Italian. Given that every 2026/2027 curriculum contains compulsory Italian-taught courses, the Italian B2 requirement is in practice unavoidable.
required_documents: EU CITIZENS AND EQUIVALENTS (admission request route): the online admission request form 'Richiesta di ammissione per le lauree magistrali in Ingegneria per l'ambiente e il territorio e Ingegneria civile 2026/27' on the UniTrento Apply portal (https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/it/Web/GoHome/ammissione/ValLmAmCivT26), which requires SPID or CIE identification for Italian adults and a guest account for foreigners or minors. The request must be submitted even by current UniTrento students and graduates who already meet the requirements, and only after having earned at least 150 ECTS. Applicants from other universities must attach a self-declaration of the examinations passed, indicating for each exam the scientific-disciplinary sector (SSD), the credits (ECTS), the date it was taken and the final grade. Evidence of English at B2 (certificate from the DICAM-recognised list, self-declaration of an English-taught degree, self-declaration of a CLA test passed, or self-declaration of being a native speaker) must be provided; where applicable, evidence of Italian. The Student Support Service then replies by e-mail stating whether additional credits must be acquired and whether an interview is required, and afterwards sends the instructions for the online enrolment application (domanda di immatricolazione) via Esse3. NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD (university-wide call): account registration on the Ammissione portal (recommended at least three working days before the deadline) followed by the online application, with the following attachments - (a) copy of the passport, personal-data pages only; (b) copy of the degree certificate, or an enrolment certificate stating the expected graduation date, officially translated into English or Italian; (c) transcript of records stating study programme, duration, grade obtained and the reference grading scale, officially translated into English or Italian; (d) certificates of any further post-graduate qualifications already obtained, with the same details and translation; (e) certificates of language and/or IT skills; (f) a curriculum vitae et studiorum IN ITALIAN drawn up in the European format; (g) the Italian language certificate, or a declaration of falling into one of the exemption cases, or a declaration of intent to sit the Italian test at UniTrento. An application fee of EUR 30 must be paid by the deadline - candidates who do not pay it are excluded and not evaluated. Up to 2 programmes may be selected. After the ranking, admitted candidates pay a non-refundable enrollment confirmation fee of EUR 100 by the date stated in the ranking, then complete the compulsory pre-enrolment ('pre-iscrizione') with the competent Italian diplomatic representation via the Universitaly portal in order to obtain the study visa, and must arrive at the University of Trento no later than 30 September 2026 or lose the admission (no extension is granted for any reason). [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: No TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT and no written entrance examination. EU CITIZENS AND EQUIVALENTS: the only possible test is an ORAL INTERVIEW (colloquio) with the Teaching Area Committee, required in three cases - (i) weighted average of the Bachelor's examinations between 22/30 and 23.99/30; (ii) a qualification belonging to a degree class other than those listed in the curricular requirements; (iii) a foreign qualification judged suitable. The Student Support Service notifies the date and format of the interview by e-mail. Separately, applicants who cannot certify English B2 must pass the English language test organised by UniTrento at the Language Centre (CLA): written part in person in Trento, oral part online, six sessions published for 2026. NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: selection is a document-based evaluation by a committee appointed by Rectoral Decree, scored out of 100 according to the criteria of Annex 1 - for Ingegneria Civile the components are evaluation of the average grade and of the time taken to graduate, evaluation of personal preparation through an interview, and evaluation of the knowledge acquired in the previous academic career in the listed subject areas. A minimum score of 50/100 is required to be declared eligible; committees may request an online interview whenever the submitted documents do not allow an adequate assessment; ties are broken in favour of the younger candidate. Non-EU candidates must also pass the pass/fail Italian language check - either the CISIA Italian L2 test with a minimum score of 52/72 (an ad hoc UniTrento session was held on 26 March 2026) or a recognised CLIQ certificate - and document English at B2 or above per Note 3 of the call. The Italian check does not contribute to the ranking score.
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027, EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: the ONLINE ADMISSION REQUEST ('richiesta di ammissione') must be submitted by 27 NOVEMBER 2026. The subsequent ENROLMENT DEADLINE ('scadenza per l'immatricolazione' / 'Enrollment deadline for a.y. 2026/2027') is 21 DECEMBER 2026. Missing curricular requirements must be made up through Single Courses for Master's Degrees with the relevant exams passed by the enrolment deadline. After receiving the matriculation number by e-mail, the student must complete the yearly enrolment ('iscrizione annuale') within 7 days in order to activate the registration and access university services. English language make-up tests at the CLA follow their own 2026 calendar with six sessions, the last registration window running 5 October to 13 November 2026 (written 23 November, oral 4 December).
application_deadline_non_eu: Academic year 2026/2027, non-EU citizens living outside Italy: application through the university-wide call, deadline 4 MARCH 2026 at 12:00 Italian time (GMT+1), with the EUR 30 application fee paid by the same date. Related milestones: deadline to pass the CISIA Italian L2 test at institutions other than UniTrento, 4 March 2026; UniTrento ad hoc CISIA Italian L2 session, 26 March 2026; publication of the ranking list on the 'Ammissione a un corso in lingua italiana' page by 24 APRIL 2026; payment of the EUR 100 non-refundable enrollment confirmation fee by the date stated in the ranking; graduation (for applicants not yet graduated) by 30 June 2026; compulsory pre-enrolment via Universitaly at the competent Italian diplomatic mission within the dates of the annual ministerial circular (published around March); final deadline to arrive at the University of Trento 30 SEPTEMBER 2026, with no extension possible. NOTE: as of the date of this research the 2026/2027 non-EU application period is closed - the official page states 'Il periodo di ammissione per l'anno accademico 2026/-2027 si e concluso, il prossimo bando di ammissione verra pubblicato indicativamente nel mese di dicembre 2026 per l'ammissione all'anno accademico 2027/2028.' Exact 2027/2028 dates were therefore not yet published.
tuition_or_fees_link: Because UniTrento classifies this programme as an Italian-language master's degree, the applicable non-EU fee page is 'Importo delle tasse per le lauree magistrali in lingua italiana': https://www.unitn.it/it/studiare/tasse-borse-alloggi/tasse/cittadini-non-europei/lauree-magistrali-italiano (English URL: https://www.unitn.it/en/study/fees-scholarships-accommodation/tuition-fees/non-eu-citizens/masters-degrees-italian). The maximum annual tuition for non-EU students is EUR 6,000 per academic year, reduced for the first year according to the admission score - 90-100/100 full exemption; 70-89.99/100 EUR 1,000; 60-69.99/100 EUR 3,000; 50-59.99/100 EUR 6,000 - and for the second year according to the credits earned by 10 August of the first year: 36 ECTS or more full exemption, 24-35 ECTS EUR 1,000, 18-23 ECTS EUR 3,000, fewer than 18 ECTS EUR 6,000; beyond the regular duration the brackets are 72+ ECTS exemption for the first extra year (EUR 1,000 per year thereafter), 48-71 ECTS EUR 1,000, 36-47 ECTS EUR 3,000, under 36 ECTS EUR 6,000. Scholarships may be awarded to top-ranked non-EU candidates scoring at least 90/100 (they include the tuition exemption and are paid only on actual arrival and stay in Italy). For EU citizens and equivalents the standard income-based (ISEE) UniTrento fee scheme applies: https://www.unitn.it/it/studiare/tasse-borse-alloggi/tasse/cittadini-europei-ed-equivalenti (fee overview: https://www.unitn.it/en/study/fees-scholarships-accommodation/tuition-fees). uncertainty_notes:
1) SCOPE DECISION (the central question in the brief). The programme should be treated as NOT English-taught. Although an English-language page exists at corsi.unitn.it/en/civil-engineering-master and the language field there reads 'English Italian', four independent official sources converge on a mixed programme with an Italian-taught compulsory core: the Programme Regulations state 'LINGUA IN CUI SI TIENE IL CORSO: italiano e inglese'; the overview page says only that 'Part of the lectures are delivered in English'; the 2026/2027 manifesti of all four curricula list Italian-named compulsory courses; and UniTrento places 'Ingegneria civile (LM23R)' in the university-wide admission call for master's degrees IN LINGUA ITALIANA, which imposes Italian B2 on non-EU applicants. The programme therefore cannot be completed entirely in English and a student without Italian would be blocked, both administratively (non-EU route) and practically (compulsory Italian courses in every curriculum).
2) COURSE-LEVEL LANGUAGE IS INFERRED, NOT TABULATED. The manifesti do not have a dedicated 'language' column. The judgement of which courses are English-taught rests on (a) two explicit notes in the Strutture manifesto ('in lingua inglese e con continuo supporto in lingua italiana'), (b) the fact that some courses keep an English title in the Italian 'Attivita formative' column while the rest are in Italian, and (c) the *** footnote marking courses shared with the Dortmund/Nantes/Trento triple Master's degree MS2. The exact English/Italian split per course should be confirmed against the individual syllabi published in Esse3 / the UniTrento course catalogue, which could not be read (see point 5). An estimate of the maximum share of ECTS obtainable in English was therefore not made.
3) POSSIBLE FULLY-ENGLISH CURRICULUM - NOT FOUND. Article 2 of the Programme Regulations refers to 'un curriculum erogato non interamente in lingua inglese', wording that implies at least one curriculum might be delivered entirely in English. No such curriculum could be identified: the 2026/2027 manifesti of all four curricula, including the English-named 'Digital Civil Infrastructure', contain Italian-titled compulsory courses. The clause appears to be either boilerplate shared across DICAM regulations or a forward-looking provision. This is the single most important residual uncertainty for the scope decision.
4) ALL FOUR MANIFESTI VERIFIED. The official 2026/2027 manifesti degli studi for all four curricula were downloaded and read in full, and all four confirm an Italian-taught compulsory core. 'Costruzioni in legno e strutture esistenti': compulsory 'Dinamica e plasticita delle strutture', 'Geotecnica e fondazioni', 'Recupero e conservazione degli edifici', 'Costruzioni in CA e CAP', 'Ingegneria sismica', 'Teoria e progetto di strutture con Laboratorio', 'Costruzioni in legno con Laboratorio', with only 'Modellazione e simulazione di strutture' flagged 'in lingua inglese e con continuo supporto in lingua italiana'. 'Progettazione integrata digitale BIM-based per le costruzioni': compulsory 'Dinamica e plasticita delle strutture', 'Geotecnica e fondazioni', 'Elettrotecnica', 'Costruzioni in CA e CAP', 'Modelli digitali per il progetto', 'Valutazione ambientale delle costruzioni', 'Gestione informatizzata del cantiere con Laboratorio', 'Architettura e tecniche per l'edilizia sostenibile con Laboratorio', 'Impianti di climatizzazione con Laboratorio', 'Teoria e progetto di strutture' or 'Costruzioni in acciaio e resistenti al fuoco'. No curriculum can be completed in English.
4b) CORROBORATION FROM THE ENGLISH-LANGUAGE ADMISSION ROUTE - WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS, STATED HONESTLY. UniTrento runs two separate non-EU admission routes. The Italian-language route is a single university-wide call with an explicit programme list that includes 'Ingegneria civile (LM23R)'. The English-language route ('Ammissione a un corso in lingua inglese') instead requires each English-taught programme to publish its own annual call on its own course site, with applications between December and March. That page mentions neither 'civil' nor 'Ingegneria civile' - but this is NOT a list from which Civil Engineering is missing, since the page publishes no list at all, so its silence is only weak evidence on its own. What makes the asymmetry meaningful is the positive fact alongside it: no English-language admission call exists for this programme anywhere, and the programme's own admission page routes non-EU applicants exclusively to the Italian-language Bando unico. Taken together with points 1-4 this corroborates the Italian-language classification; taken alone it would not.
5) ACCESS LIMITATIONS. corsi.unitn.it serves HTTP 405 to every direct request and presents an interactive 'Human Verification' bot check in a browser; www.unitn.it returns HTTP 403; infostudenti.unitn.it returns HTTP 503; offertaformativa.unitn.it returns 503/302; unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it returns 405. No bot check was circumvented. All content from those hosts was read through the Internet Archive, mostly via freshly requested Save-Page-Now captures made on 31 August 2026 (admission page 20260831194941, English admission page 20260831194603, overview 20260831194833, documents page 20260831194634, non-EU call page 20260831201001, plus the Regolamento, Strutture and DCI manifesto, Allegato 1 table, Bando and fee-page PDFs/captures). www.dicam.unitn.it and webapps.unitn.it were directly reachable; the UniTrento Apply portal pages require SPID/CIE or guest-account login, so the internal content of the admission forms could not be inspected.
6) EU-SIDE DOCUMENT LIST IS NOT EXHAUSTIVELY PUBLISHED. For EU citizens and equivalents the official page describes the online admission request and the self-declaration of examinations (SSD, ECTS, date, grade), but does not publish a formal document checklist comparable to the non-EU call; further documents may be requested by the Student Support Service case by case. The exact list of DICAM-recognised English certificates is in a separate PDF (certificazioni-internazionali-riconosciute-dicam-2024.pdf) that could not be downloaded because of archive rate limiting.
7) FEE PAGE VERSIONING. The non-EU fee page retrieved on 31 August 2026 is headed 'Importi tasse 2025/2026', but its brackets are identical to those written into the 2026/2027 call (Art. 7), so the figures are current. Exact EUR amounts of the ISEE-based fees for EU citizens and equivalents were not retrieved; only the landing pages are cited.
8) NON-EU CYCLE ALREADY CLOSED. The 2026/2027 non-EU application window (deadline 4 March 2026) had closed before this research and the ranking outcomes were already published (Allegato2_esitiLMITA.pdf, April 2026). The next call, for a.y. 2027/2028, is announced for around December 2026; its dates, quota and possible changes to the Italian/English requirements are not yet published, and the 5-place quota should not be assumed to carry over.
9) CURRICULUM NAMING DRIFT. The curriculum called 'Riabilitazione' (Rehabilitation) in the 2025/2026 manifesti was renamed 'Costruzioni in legno e strutture esistenti' from 2026/2027, and 'Progettazione integrata e digitale' became 'Progettazione integrata digitale BIM based per le costruzioni'. The English marketing pages still use 'Rehabilitation' and 'Integrated Digital Design', which do not match the official Italian names in the regulations and manifesti.
10) BIENNIAL COURSE ROTATION. 'Opere di sostegno' and 'Elementi di meccanica delle rocce e costruzioni in sotterraneo' alternate on a two-year cycle (the latter is noted as 'attivo nell'a.a. 2027/28'), and a curriculum may be deactivated if it does not attract enough enrolments, so the offer verified here may differ in later intakes.
